title: Why Ice Cubes Are Cloudy
description:
Why ice cubes are cloudy: tap water carries air you can't see, but ice has almost no room for it. In a freezer a cube freezes from the outside in, so every new layer of ice pushes the air towards the middle. The middle freezes last and the air has nowhere to go, so it is trapped as tiny bubbles that scatter light: that's the white cloud. A still lake freezes from the top down, the air escapes, and lake ice can be crystal clear. Freeze water from one side only and you get the same clear ice.

Have you ever made a perfectly clear ice cube?

More true whys: https://www.youtube.com/@truewhys?sub_confirmation=1

Sources: Purdue University Materials Engineering, "Got Materials? Clear ice"; Indiana Public Media, A Moment of Science: "The secret behind getting clear ice cubes"; Cook's Illustrated, "What is clear ice and how can I make it at home?".
